pr.title: Give links to trip.here a social card image
pr.head: cc114fcce2348164b67c8ac2140065d098f671f1

summary: site/ is trip.here, the project's one-page website. It is hand-written HTML with no build step, and Vercel deploys the site/ directory as it stands.

When someone pastes https://trip.here/ into Slack, X, iMessage, or another app that previews links, the app reads the page's Open Graph tags to draw the preview. The page already had a title and a description, but no image, so the preview had none. This change adds a 1200 by 630 card image and the tags that point to it.

The card copies the page's dark design: the bold monospace trip wordmark with its orange block cursor, the tagline, a shortened version of the page's trip enter transcript, and the install command along the bottom. Its source, site/og.html, stays in the repository so the card can be edited and rendered again, and site/.vercelignore keeps that source off the live site.
The branch's first commit tried a card under .github/ with a .projector.toml setting, and the second commit removed both. Only the four files under site/ differ from main.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Open Graph tags: og: meta tags in the page's head that tell link previews what title, description, and image to show.
  • Social card: the image a link preview shows, conventionally 1200 by 630 pixels.
  • .vercelignore: a list of files Vercel leaves out of a deployment, read from the project's root directory.

cards.title: What the review checked
cards.html:
• Rendering og.html with its documented command produces a PNG byte-identical to og.png.
  • The branch's Vercel preview serves the five new tags, serves /og.png as image/png, and returns 404 for /og.
  • The card's chooser lines match what trip enter prints and fit the card.
  • The review found no blocking problems.

groups.title: The tags that point at the card
groups.kicker: Five meta tags in the page's head
intro: The page's head gains the tags a link preview reads to find an image. og:image gives the image's address, og:image:width and og:image:height give its size so a preview can lay itself out before the image loads, and og:image:alt describes it for screen readers. twitter:card set to summary_large_image asks X for the wide preview rather than a small thumbnail.
The existing title, description, and og:url tags are unchanged.

files.note: Adds the image tags and the twitter:card tag beside the existing Open Graph tags.

checks.text: og:image names the production address, not a relative path, because link previews need an absolute URL. A preview deployment's tags therefore still point at https://trip.here/og.png, so a link-preview validator shows the card only after this merges.
The width and height match the image: file site/og.png reports 1200 by 630.
X falls back to the Open Graph title, description, and image when its own twitter: tags are absent, so this one tag is all it needs.

groups.title: The card and its source
groups.kicker: The image, the HTML it is rendered from, and the file that keeps that HTML off the site
intro: og.png is the card itself, served at https://trip.here/og.png. It is a screenshot of og.html, a fixed 1200 by 630 page that reuses the site's colors and font stacks. To change the card, edit og.html and run the headless Chrome command in its comment, which overwrites og.png.

Without .vercelignore, Vercel would deploy og.html too, and the site's cleanUrls setting would serve it at trip.here/og. The ignore file sits in site/ because that directory, which holds vercel.json, is the Vercel project's root.

checks.text: On the branch's Vercel preview, /og.png returns 200 with content-type: image/png and the same bytes as the committed file, /og returns 404, and /og.html redirects to that 404.

files.note: The card's source, with the command that renders it. Render it on a Mac, where the font stacks resolve to the fonts the site uses.

checks.text: Running the command in this comment against this head produced a PNG byte-identical to the committed og.png, so the image is current.
The chooser lines match what trip enter prints in src/client/mod.rs, ↑/↓ + enter · 0-9 · q cancels and (new session), and the rendered card shows both in full inside the terminal panel.
